lessons.title: Rude but common
explanation: ⚠️ **18+ content.** You need to *understand* these words, because you'll hear them constantly. Know when **not** to use them.
**Severity scale:** 0 clean · 1 mild · 2 rude · 3 strong · 4 extremely offensive.
**gatvol** (2) — fed up. Literally "arse-full". Super common, but not with teachers or grandparents. Safer: **moeg vir**, **sat vir**.
**kak** (2) — crap. Very common in casual speech. **Dis kak!** Safer: **sleg**, **nonsens**.
**bliksem** (2) — to hit; also "damn!". **Ek sal jou bliksem!** is a threat.
**voetsek** (2) — get lost. Originally for chasing dogs away; very rude to a person.

examples.af: Ek is gatvol vir die reën.
examples.en: I'm fed up with the rain.

examples.af: Ek is moeg vir die reën.

lessons.title: Strong swearing — recognise, don't repeat
explanation: **fok / fokken** (3) — the f-word and its intensifier. Very strong.
**befok** (3) — crazy, or (positively) awesome. **Is jy befok?** = Are you f***ing crazy?
**doos** (3) — standard meaning *box*; as an insult it's strong and vulgar ("idiot").
**poes** (4) — one of the most offensive words in the language. Shocking in almost any setting.
Mild alternatives that won't get you in trouble: **jislaaik!**, **sies!**, **ag nee!**

⛔ **Slurs**: Afrikaans also has racial and homophobic slurs from the apartheid era. They're in the dictionary (18+) only so you can recognise them. Some have led to criminal convictions in South Africa. Never use them.
